The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 for claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/-.

2. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is that, on 22-02-2024 at about 10.00a.m. she was crossing the Whitefield Main Road, near Garudacharyapalya Metro Station, at that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.DL-6/SBG-2773 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life, came at high speed from Tin Factory towards Hoodi and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident, due to forced impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Manipal Hospital, K.R. Puram,
wherein she was treated as an inpatient, the petitioner had sustained comminuted fracture both bones left leg with fracture base of 2nd metatarsal and other injuries.

On 23-02-2024 she undergone operation of closed reduction and internal fixation left tibia for both bone fracture left leg and closed reduction, K-wire pinning lisfranc fracture dislocation left foot and was discharged on 29-02-2024 with an advice of regular follow up treatment and medications.
So far petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other charges.

The injuries sustained in the accident have not healed and she is not able to do regular activities and undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings, since, the injuries caused are permanent in nature.
4. It is further stated that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 49 years, she was working as a Counselor at Rehab Center and earning Rs.35,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries, she is not able to discharge her work and has lost the earnings for lead down period and she is facing great financial difficulties.

5. It is stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence act of the rider of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.DL-6/SBG-2773, against whom the Mahadevapura Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.25/2024 P/U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
Hence, respondent No.1 being the Owner and respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.

7. Respondent No.2 in its objection to the main petition contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence, it is liable to be dismissed in limine.
It has not admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its force as on the date of accident.
It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have effective and valid DL to drive the same and as such respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further contended that, there was no negligence on the part of the alleged rider of the alleged insured vehicle in issue as he was proceeding with due care and cautious by following traffic rules and regulations.
On the contrary, it is specifically submitted that the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner herself.

Further, Respondent No.2 has denied the accident, age,
income and also the amount spent towards medical expenses by the petitioner.
It has further contended that the compensation and interest claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, on all these grounds, it has sought for dismissal of the petition.

8. On basis of the pleadings and materials, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether petitioner proves that on 22-02- 2024 at about 10.00 AM, she was crossing the Whitefield Main Road, near Garudacharpalya Metro Station, at that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.DL-6/SBG-2773 drove it, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came at high speed from T.N. Factory towards Hoodi and dashed against petitioner and caused the accident, due to said forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
if so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.3 and got marked 02 documents as per Ex.P.18 and P.19.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any oral evidence and not marked any documents on their sides.

10. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials available on hand.
11.

The petitioner filed this petition against the respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident, that occurred on 22-02-2024.

In the cross-examination she has stated that, the accident was took place at the time of crossing the road while she was going to shop from her house.
Further stated that, by observing both sides she was started to cross the road and almost crossed the road at that time bike was hit suddenly.
Further denied that, due to her fault, the accident was took place.
14. The petitioner got examined the Medical Record Officer as PW.2 and got marked 04 documents as Ex.P.14(a) to 17.
Ex. P.14(a) is the Authorization Letter, Ex.P.15 is the Police Intimation, Ex.P.16 is the MLC Register and Ex.P.17 is the Inpatient Records.

Ex.P.18 is the Clinical Examination Report and Ex.P.19 is the X-rays with reports.

On perusal of Ex.P.4 the Sketch it appears that, the petitioner was crossed almost of the road and she is just near to the end of the road and offending vehicle hit her, though there was a sufficient space for moving the offending vehicle on its right side of the road, the driver of offending vehicle took his vehicle to his left side and dashed to the petitioner and caused the accident.

21. ISSUE No.2:-
The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificate at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.10 to 12 discharge summaries issued by Manipal Hospitals, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.

On perusal of the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.6, it is discloses that the petitioner has sustained (1) Left Leg tibia bones fracture,
(2) Left foot fibula 2nd and 3rd metatarsal bones fracture, (3) Acute submarine pulmonary embolism.
On perusal of the said injuries, the Doctor has opinion that the injuries are grievous in nature.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.10 discharge summary, wherein the diagnosis that, comminuted fracture both bone left leg with fracrure base of 2nd metatarsal S/P - closed reduction and internal fixation left tibia, closed reduction and K wire pinning lisfranc fracture dislocation left foot done on 23-02-2024 under GA Acute submassive pulmonary embolism (Provoked).
Normal biventribular function.
Mild PAH and admitted on 22-02-2024 and discharged on 29-02-2024.
Ex.P.11 discharge summary, wherein the diagnosis that, Tibia ILN left tibia and admitted on 25-03-2024 and discharged on 26-03-2024.
Ex.P.12 discharge summary, wherein the diagnosis that, delay in union of Tibia fracture and admitted on 26-07-2024 and discharged on 26-07-2024.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, as petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and admitted in the hospital, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
22. The petitioner produced medical bills, which are marked as Ex.P.14.

As per the said bills, Sl.
No.6 and 22 are the advance receipts, Sl.No.7, 8, 10, 13, 15 and 20 are the duplicate copies of the bills, hence, they have not been considered.
The respondents have not disputed the other medical bills.

On perusal of the said medical bills and also considering the remaining bills and also treatment taken by the petitioner in the hospital, the petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bills amount of Rs.1,44,725/- under the head of medical expenditure.

23. As per Ex.P.10 to 12 discharge summaries the petitioner took treatment at Manipal Hospital,
Bangalore from 22-02-2024 to 29-02-2024, from 25-03-2024 to 26- 03-2024 and from 26-07-2024 to 26-07-2024 i.e., for 11 days.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.11,000/- under the head Transportation, food,

24. The Petitioner contended that, due to injuries she was suffering from pain and mental agony and she is unable to carry on his day to day activities which she used to do prior to the accident.
To prove the assessment of disability, the petitioner got examined one Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW-3.

In the chief examination affidavit PW.3 deposed that, on 14-07-2025 the petitioner came to him for assessment of disability purpose and on examination he found that, (i) infection (ii) deformity (iii)
loss of sensation are present and patient always limps while walking and walk slowly.

Radiological X-rays examination revealed that, comminuted fracture of tibia and fibula of left leg shows union with implants in situ in tibia and lisfranc's fracture dislocation shows union of fractures.
He examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically and assessed the total disability of the left lower limb at 40.70% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 20.35%.
In the cross-examination admitted that, he is not a treated doctor, he has not consulted the treated doctor, he has seen the case sheet of Manipal Hospital.
The fractures are united.
The petitioner was limping and walking slowly with the support.
However by considering the nature of the wounds, condition of the petitioner and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has considered the disability of the Petitioner at 15% to the whole body.

25. The petitioner stated that, at the time of accident she was aged about 49 years and she was working as Councelor at Rehab Center and she used to earn a sum of Rs.35,000/-p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, she cannot do any work as earlier.
The petitioner has not produced any documents to prove her income and avocation.
Therefore, in present days the coolie worker get Rs.500/- to Rs.600/- per day.
This accident is of the year 2024.
However, by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/-.
26. As per Ex.P.13 Notarized Copy of Adhar Card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 10-07-1974.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is taken as 50 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 13 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,500 x 12 x 13 x 15% = Rs.3,86,100/-
Hence, this Tribunal award Rs.3,86,100/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
27.
The petitioner also sought for expenses towards future medicine for further treatment.
In the chief- examination affidavit the petitioner deposed that, she is forced to spent huge amount for future medication.
PW.3 doctor deposed in the chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant from tibia of left leg.
In the cross-examination, PW.3 admitted that he had not treated the petitioner and fractures are united.

However, by considering the age and nature of injuries and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal has award reasonable compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head future medical expenses (Which does not carry any interest).

31. Interest:

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20- 03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru has held Monica Ponetti Lokesh vs Gourav Arora on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62455923/
7 that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.

32. Liability:-
 Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.DL-6/SBG-2773.

As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle, hence,
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Further,
Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
33. ISSUE No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.7,41,825/- with interest @ 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of the petitioner with proper identification.
(As the petitioner has to incur some more amount for future medical expenses) Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

7 that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest that can be awarded on Judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a. and that since Sec.149 of M.V. Act provides for the interest on Judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a.
and not more than that.
Hence, this Court has hold that the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
32. Liability:-
 Respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.DL-6/SBG-2773.
As discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending vehicle, hence,
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.
